label: a1-led-to-S2 (rare a1) at D2, or GO after an unrewarded trial; early-episode only
explanation: Two input-driven clauses, both observed, and both gated by episode time. (1) At D2 it fires only when the input shows choice a1 and state S2, i.e. a rare transition after a1 (about 55% of the activation mass; it never fires for a1->S1, a2->S2 or a2->S1). (2) At GO it fires almost only when the previous trial was unrewarded (in_rew = 0 at D1; it never fires on steps with a rewarded input), about 45% of the mass. It never fires at D1. Rates fall steadily with ep_trial: highest in trials 0-9, near zero after trial 60 and absent after 70, and the GO clause fades sooner than the D2 clause, hence the different cutoffs. This looks like an early-episode or learning-phase uncertainty unit. Within GO it does not track the upcoming action cleanly: restricting to action==1 lowers recall. The main shortfall is precision (about 0.66 on dev): many unrewarded-GO and a1->S2 steps early in the episode stay inactive, so a hidden-state factor not captured here also gates it. Magnitude is largest on the D2 a1->S2 steps (top-quartile coverage is about 1.0). Dev: F1 0.77, mass recall 0.97.
